item.research_question: How can a one-dimensional (1D) medium-entropy magnetic alloy be rationally designed to facilitate electromagnetic wave attenuation capability in the low-frequency (2–6 GHz) microwave absorption field?
item.material_system: FeCoNi medium-entropy alloy nanoparticles (FeCoNi NP) embedded in a one-dimensional carbon fiber (CF) matrix, specifically FeCoNi/CF-1, FeCoNi/CF-2, and FeCoNi/CF-3; atomic ratios of Fe, Co, and Ni varied (e.g., Fe50Co50, Fe50Co40Ni10, Fe40Co40Ni20).
item.processing_route: FeCoNi NPs synthesized via low-temperature hydrothermal process (120 °C for 12 h) using FeCl2·4H2O, CoCl2·6H2O, NiCl2·6H2O, NaOH, and N2H4·H2O; NPs dispersed in polyacrylonitrile (PAN)/DMF solution; electrospinning at 14.0 kV, 20 cm distance, 0.45 mL h−1; pre-oxidation at 240 °C for 1.5 h followed by 330 °C for 0, 1, or 1.5 h; annealing in H2/Ar (5%) at 700 °C for 2 h with a ramping rate of 5 °C min−1.
item.test_conditions: Electromagnetic wave absorption performance evaluated via coaxial-line method in the 2–6 GHz frequency range; reflection loss (RL) measured with absorber thickness ranging from 1 to 5 mm; magnetic properties characterized using superconducting quantum interference device magnetometry and vector network analyzer; off-axis electronic holography used to evaluate magnetic field lines.
key_findings: The FeCoNi/CF-1 exhibits an effective absorption band (fE) of 1.3 GHz in the low-frequency electromagnetic field at an ultrathin thickness of 2 mm.
The saturation magnetization (Ms) of FeCoNi/CF-1 is 194.0 emu g−1 with a coercivity (Hc) of 107.4 Oe, demonstrating desirable soft ferromagnetic nature.
The average level of imaginary magnetic permeability (μ′′) for FeCoNi/CF-1 is 1.4, significantly higher than the 0.2 limit of most previous literature materials.
The real part of permittivity for FeCoNi/CF-1 is enlarged to 5 times that of pure carbon fibers, while the imaginary part is 3 times higher.
The ID/IG value in Raman spectroscopy for FeCoNi/CF-1 decreased to 1.25 compared to 1.28 for pure CF, indicating increased graphitization.
Magnetic permeability of FeCoNi/CF-2 and FeCoNi/CF-3 exhibited slightly higher values compared to FeCoNi/CF-1, attributed to higher magnetic-carbon ratios.
Magnetic parameters (μ′ and μ′′) reached a maximum range when Ni content was in the middle range (4%–14%).
item.mechanism: The enhanced EM wave absorption is attributed to the construction of a one-dimensional magnetic network that increases shape anisotropy and promotes magnetic response, alongside the intrinsic physical features of the medium-entropy alloy which improve magnetic-domain movement. The 1D structure facilitates high-density and continuous magnetic coupling networks where magnetic field lines radiate between adjacent particles, causing frequent domain wall migration and phase lag between internal magnetic moments and external fields. Additionally, the FeCoNi alloy acts as a catalyst for graphitization, enhancing electrical conductivity and dielectric loss, while the medium-entropy design intrinsically upgrades magnetic loss capacity through ferromagnetic resonance and natural loss.
item.limitations: The text notes that in the lower-frequency region (2–6 GHz), it is difficult to decouple between impedance matching and EM wave attenuation, which often leads to poor performance in other materials. Furthermore, extending the pre-oxidation time indefinitely causes the carbon content to decrease, leading to a drop in dielectric constant that is not conducive to excellent absorbing properties.
item.future_work: The study opens up a new method for the design and preparation of high-performance 1D magnetic EM absorbers and suggests that the unique 1D shape can be further applied to other magnetic structures which require good shape anisotropy.
quotes: The designed one-dimensional FeCoNi/CF exhibits excellent performance, with a broad effective absorption band of 1.3 GHz in the low-frequency electromagnetic field at an ultrathin thickness of 2 mm.

The 1D-shaped FeCoNi alloy embedded composite demonstrates the high-density and continuous magnetic network using off-axis electronic holography technique, indicating the excellent magnetic loss ability under an external EM field.
